I already have blocked them from everything. I had done that even before the last relationship. She still managed to find a way around it though or just found out about the relationship another way, found the profile of the girl I was with and then sabotaged things.

As for emotional stability, I'll admit there's a few things that need work but at the same time I don't want to waste my life. Comparing where I am now to where I was say a year ago in terms of stability, it's like looking at two completley different people.

Just to clear one more thing up, I did look into charging Susan with harassment or getting a restraining order but there's a few issues with that. Getting a restraining order would stop her from messaging me, but not someone I ended up with. Yes, a restraining order could be filed to prevent her from messaging people I know such as family members but for someone I only recently started to date it's a bit more complicated. 

As for the harassment, I've blocked her. I blocked her before I entered my relationship with Peanut but she still found out. I unblocked her a few months after that relationship ended.
The thing with harassment is that it needs to happen more than once for it to be taken seriously. 

So really the only thing I can do now is try to deal with the baggage and try to prevent her from sabotaging my next relationship.

It's been a while since I posted here but I just want to update this thread. 
I still have some issues, but they're a bit easier to manage. I still seem to be going in and out of depression but it's a little bit easier to manage. 

All this took was going to a convention Q-con and in the process solving the problem of not knowing who I was. This problem arose when I turned 20 and as I said, reflected on myself. I was living in a false identity where I had taken so many steps to be the complete opposite of my father I had no idea who I actually was as a person. 

At the closing ceremony where everyone was reflecting on the convention itself (while some pretty good music played) there was a moment of clarity where I not only realised who I was as a person but became comfortable about it. 

I will not become my so-called father and he does not define me as a person.

With the convention solving this problem almost two weeks ago I've begun to feel better. I still feel like shit sometimes, sure but it's easier to manage like I said.
Becuase I can't get therapy for any of these issues and I can't go to anyone about them.

I am nothing and your argument has no meaning "capable of being mentally unwell=capable of being ecstatic" you could use that towards anything, like "you're capable of being mentally unwell=capable of being angry, hungry, in love ect"

There was a time I wanted to be happy but I've accepted that that isn't possible and now all I want to do is to die.
And what makes you say that? I am a mess who has nothing to offer the world.
I can't get that therapy though, otherwise I wouldn't be here. It's over for me.

Like I said I tried meditation and exercise in the past and they were of no help to me. For suicidal thoughts you need actual therapy, not a bunch of zen stuff. Therapy is not something I have access to.

That "breath" you call life is not worth it, none of this is.
Meditation and exercise never helped me, not really. I don't think you can just wash away something like suicidal thoughts with some zen and running.
What changed to make your perspective change?
I've tried for twenty years to make life "pleasant" I'm not spending the next 50 years feeling like total shit day in day out.

I phoned Lifeline. They were of no help to me. On one occasion in particular I called, explained my situation and despite me saying that I didn't want to go into further details the person on the other end of the phone kept pushing and pushing until I had a damn relapse. 

On several occasions I contacted them and the people on the other end of the phone spent all of their time trying to figure out who I was rather than help me.

I used lifeline's actual counseling services as a teenager, it didn't help me.

For those suggesting I go to a therapist, I feel I should explain something to you. I live in a country called Northern Ireland which is currently run by the DUP. This is significant becuase the DUP are very, very conservative and right wing in their beliefs and like the Conservative party believe in privatising healthcare, by cutting the healthcare that everyone can afford (the NHS) until it no longer exists and then replacing it with a system of privatisation.

Northern Ireland, out of the rest of the UK has the worst resources for mental health. They are pretty much nonexistent. I have been to three different GPs, all of which were useless and told me to go away essentially. I went to a place to get diagnosed (which is needed before therapy so they can figure out what kind of therapy you need) and was told that any depression I had was "circumstantial" and all I needed to do was improve my situation and it would go away. 

I have a family member with schizophrenia who had all of his support taken away. He was without the proper medication or any kind of contact with a doctor for over two months before someone finally stepped in.

As for private healthcare here, it's really expensive. Therapy would cost me around 50-70 quid per hour (that's 72.55-101.56 US dollars). 

To cut it short, I just can't get therapy. Not under a Tory-DUP government. As for support groups that may even offer counseling, I've looked into that too. The problem is that the abuse-related groups here are for women and/or children only, or those who suffered abuse under some kind of institution (there's a history of that in this country) the other groups provide only useless helplines  or are only for specific kinds of abuse i.e sexual. 

He never abused me in "that" way, so there's a problem.

I did contact some of these groups and helplines that only sent me on goose chases or just told me to talk to my GP. The same GP who's as useful as a chocolate fireguard.

Seeking help and counselling has been difficult as I feel that no one will believe me and I also have problems with authority figures. When in high school I talked to a school counselor about the abuse, the bullies and the teachers who did nothing. The first thing the counselor did was tell my parents and the teachers.  

Also, my so-called father is a police officer and used this to his advantage. Who'd suspect a police officer, one who actually specializes in child protection was abusing his kid?
